title: Deposit Money Set Against an Event Bill at Settlement
content:
Deposit money standing against a Private Event & Banquet Services booking is set against the amount billed at settlement rather than before the bill is issued, and where that money reaches the amount billed the whole of the amount billed is met from it, the surplus being returned rather than carried.

## The deposit money the settlement draws on

The deposit money the settlement draws on is what the agreement's event ledger shows taken in deposits, less anything already set against a bill and less anything already returned.

## What comes off

1. Where deposit money stands against the booking and reaches the amount billed, the whole of the amount billed comes off what is settled, the surplus being returned rather than carried.
2. Where deposit money stands against the booking and falls short of the amount billed, all of that money comes off what is settled.
3. Where no deposit money stands against the booking, nothing comes off on that account.

| Deposit money standing against the booking | Comes off what is settled |
| --- | --- |
| More than the amount billed | The amount billed, the surplus being returned |
| Exactly the amount billed | The amount billed |
| Less than the amount billed | All of that deposit money |
| None | Nothing |

## Worked illustration on hypothetical records

An agreement's event ledger shows 6400 taken in deposits on a booking, 1200 already set against an earlier bill and 400 already returned, so 4800 stands against the booking. Against an amount billed of 7250, the 4800 falls short, and all 4800 comes off what is settled. Against an amount billed of 4300, the 4800 reaches it, so 4300 comes off and what is left over is returned rather than carried.
